guards.old:
A nonempty connected tree of $c\ge1$ rational
normalization components has Euler number
$c+1\ge2$, including any unibranch singular
points. Additivity gives $e(S)\ge3$.
guards.new:
Let $P=\{p\in C:\#\nu_C^{-1}(p)>1\}$ and put
$r_p=\#\nu_C^{-1}(p)$ for $p\in P$. The tree has
$c+\#P$ vertices and $\sum_{p\in P}r_p$ edges, so
$\sum_p(r_p-1)=c-1$. Thus
\[
 e(C)=2c-\sum_p(r_p-1)=c+1\ge2.
\]
Unibranch singular points have one preimage and contribute
zero to the subtraction. Finally
$e(S)=e(S_{\rm reg})+e(C)\ge3$.
guards.reason: Explain the branch count in the same Euler computation. The finite normalization quotient identifies exactly r_p points at p, lowering Euler characteristic by r_p−1. This includes arbitrary analytic singularities with those fibres; unibranch fibres make no subtraction. Compactly supported additivity agrees with ordinary Euler number on the oriented four-dimensional smooth stratum.
